name: oxid
_readme: OXID eShop as migration target (self-hosted PHP shop, CE/PE/EE, Twig themes from v7, optional GraphQL modules) and as source (a client can plausibly be running an OXID 6.x/7.x shop today, and the module conventions - metadata.php, source/modules, the class chain - are well defined and inspectable). Seed from general OXID knowledge; everything is a hypothesis until verified per engagement.

as_target.default_frontend: shipped server-rendered Twig theme (Apex in v7, Flow in v6) - headless requires the GraphQL modules plus a self-built frontend

snippets.critic2_persona: senior solution architect who has delivered several OXID eShop projects in the DACH market, is OXID-certified, and knows exactly what is Community, Professional, Enterprise or B2B edition, what the GraphQL modules do and do not cover, and how the module class chain behaves under load of many modules
snippets.docs_domains: docs.oxid-esales.com (developer and admin documentation, module development, module certification, upgrade guides, compilation/edition matrix), github.com/OXID-eSales (oxideshop-ce, oxideshop-metapackage-*, graphql-base, graphql-storefront, doctrine-migration-wrapper - releases and CHANGELOG.md are the reliable version source), exchange.oxid-esales.com (module and theme marketplace, module compatibility per compilation), oxid-esales.com (editions, licensing, partner list). Version facts belong in the GitHub CHANGELOG or the docs compilation matrix, not on marketing pages.
snippets.best_practice: extend via the metadata.php extend chain and always call parent (class MyClass extends MyClass_parent) or, from 6.5/7 onwards, decorate the shop service in the module services.yaml - never patch a class under vendor/oxid-esales; add data via a Doctrine migration in the module's migration/ folder, not via onActivate SQL that cannot be replayed; keep template changes as named block overrides in metadata.php blocks instead of replacing whole template files, so a compilation upgrade only breaks the block; module settings via metadata.php settings so they land in var/configuration and are deployable; anything read from a controller must survive the file-based cache - clear it explicitly after a configuration change.
snippets.critic2_focus: D1: compilation/edition facts (which feature is CE vs PE vs EE vs B2B Edition), version numbers from the GitHub CHANGELOG, deprecations across the 6.x -> 7.x jump (Smarty -> Twig, module configuration DB -> YAML). D2: is the claimed standard counterpart really shipped in the metapackage of that edition, or an Exchange module by a partner. D3: does the standard edition in scope really cover it, or does it need the B2B Edition licence, an Exchange module or custom work. D4: which GraphQL query/mutation actually exists in the graphql-storefront version in scope, and whether the CMS content the requirement needs is exposed over the API at all.
snippets.expected_hotspots_d3: check whether the following are covered by the edition in scope rather than assumed: headless or app frontends (GraphQL module coverage, especially checkout, payment and CMS content); multi-shop (Enterprise edition only - verify); the B2B feature set (company accounts, budgets, approval workflows, RFQ, order templates, punchout/OCI) which sits in the separately licensed B2B Edition; customer-specific price agreements beyond price groups and graduated prices; live ERP price and stock calls inside the storefront request; faceted search and merchandising relevance (needs an Elasticsearch/Solr module - verify which is certified for the compilation); product configurators and made-to-order products; PIM-grade attribute governance and workflows; personalisation and segmentation; subscriptions; returns/RMA self-service.
snippets.expected_blockers_d4: check before committing: which GraphQL queries and mutations the graphql-storefront version in scope really exposes (checkout, payment method selection, CMS content and B2B entities are the usual gaps - verify per module release); no first-party REST storefront or admin API in the metapackage, so REST requirements imply a partner or custom module; the module class chain has no equivalent on a headless or SaaS target, so every _parent override is re-implementation work; a 6.x -> 7.x move rewrites every Smarty template override to Twig; module configuration moved from the database to var/configuration YAML at 6.2, so older shops carry activation state the repository cannot show; the module and partner ecosystem is DACH-centric, so a non-DACH payment, tax or carrier requirement often has no certified module; Visual CMS content blocks are module-owned data structures, not core CMS pages.
snippets.content_model_notes: Core content is oxcontent records: CMS pages and CMS snippets (idents referenced from templates and emails) with per-language columns - plain rich text, no component tree. Editorial page composition comes from the Visual CMS module (Professional/Enterprise - verify the licence), which stores widget/content blocks per CMS page and renders them through theme templates; those blocks exist only as long as the module is licensed and active. Theme-level composition is Twig block overrides declared in metadata.php blocks - developer artefacts, not editable by business users. Category and product long descriptions are the third place editorial content hides. Nothing in this model has a documented headless render contract: a GraphQL-fed frontend gets content/contents as HTML strings and must render them itself, and Visual CMS blocks are typically not exposed at all (verify).
snippets.api_families_hint: see knowledge target_api_endpoint_families - OXID GraphQL is delivered by the optional graphql-base + graphql-storefront modules, not by the core metapackage; entity coverage must be checked per module release

as_source.language_stack: PHP 8.x, Symfony components, Doctrine DBAL/migrations, MySQL/MariaDB; Twig templates from v7, Smarty in v6
as_source.default_frontend: server-rendered theme (Apex in v7, Flow in v6) with module block overrides
do_not_run: module installation, activation or deactivation of any kind
composer install/update, shop setup or any DB-touching script

snippets.version_markers: root composer.json / composer.lock: the metapackage constraint oxid-esales/oxideshop-metapackage-ce|-pe|-ee is the AUTHORITATIVE compilation version (the edition is encoded in the package name); oxid-esales/oxideshop-ce version in composer.lock is the platform release inside that compilation. Cross-check vendor/oxid-esales/oxideshop-ce/source/Core/ShopVersion.php and Core/Edition* for the runtime version and edition. Per module: metadata.php $sMetadataVersion (2.0 / 2.1 - the version decides which metadata keys are honoured) and $aModule['version']. PHP version from composer.json require.php. Template engine: presence of source/Application/views/**/*.tpl means Smarty (6.x), *.html.twig means Twig (7.x) - a repository with both is mid-migration.
snippets.active_units_config: AUTHORITATIVE from 6.2 onwards = var/configuration/shops/<shopId>.yaml: each module appears with its configuration and its activation state; a directory under source/modules that appears in no shop YAML is DEAD. var/configuration/environment/*.yaml carries environment overrides. Before 6.2 the activation state lived in database rows (oxconfig aModules / aDisabledModules / oxconfig module-namespaced values) which a code-only analysis CANNOT see - then the activation list must be requested from the client as an export, and until it arrives no module may be called dead. In a multi-shop (Enterprise) installation the state is PER SHOP: a module can be active in shop 1 and inactive in shop 2, so count activations per shop before scoping.
snippets.package_sources: root composer.json require: modules published as composer type oxideshop-module, placed into source/modules/<vendor>/<module> by oxid-esales/oxideshop-composer-plugin (extra.oxideshop.target-directory in the module's composer.json decides the path, so the folder name is not the package name); composer.lock for the pinned versions; themes as type oxideshop-theme; Exchange marketplace modules are often vendored into source/modules without a composer entry - treat a module folder with no matching composer.lock entry as manually vendored and unpatchable.
snippets.override_mechanisms: overridden = the metadata.php extend map inserts a module class into the CLASS CHAIN of a shop class (virtual namespace OxidEsales\Eshop\... => the module class). The module class must declare `extends <MyClass>_parent`; that alias is generated at runtime and points at the PREVIOUS link of the chain, i.e. the next module or finally the shop class. Consequences to check per finding: (1) chain ORDER is the module activation order recorded in var/configuration/shops/<shopId>.yaml, not the folder order - reordering changes behaviour with no code change; (2) a module method that does not call parent::<method>() silently cuts off every module below it in the chain, which is the classic OXID conflict and produces no error; (3) two modules extending the same class and the same method are a latent conflict even when both call parent, if both mutate the same output. shadowed = a class file inside a module declaring a FQN under OxidEsales\Eshop\* or replacing an autoloaded vendor class - overlays the shop class on the classpath outside the chain mechanism. decorated = from 6.5/7 onwards a module services.yaml that decorates or aliases a shop service (Symfony DI) - the modern replacement for the class chain and the one to prefer in a target design. controllers = metadata.php controllers map registers a controller key usable as cl=<key>, and re-using an existing key overrides that route. templates = metadata.php templates map replaces a WHOLE template file (upgrade-hostile). blocks = metadata.php blocks inject or override a named block region of a theme template; several modules on the same block are applied in chain order and additive by position. events = onActivate/onDeactivate callbacks that run SQL - a side effect the repository shows but whose result is only in the database.
snippets.schema_sources: module migration/ folder with Doctrine migration classes (oxid-esales/doctrine-migration-wrapper) is the sanctioned schema source; metadata.php events onActivate SQL and stray *.sql files under the module's setup/install folder are the unsanctioned ones - count both. Schema deltas take two shapes: extra columns on standard tables (oxarticles, oxuser, oxorder, oxcategories, ...) and new module tables (usually <vendor><module>_* prefixed). Multi-language columns are duplicated per shop language with _1, _2, ... suffixes and Enterprise adds oxarticles_set1..setN extension tables plus per-shop views (oxv_*) that must be regenerated - so one logical field can be many physical columns. Views (oxv_*) are generated, never edited.
snippets.workflow_sources: OXID ships no workflow or process engine: order state is fields on oxorder plus the steps inside oxOrder::finalizeOrder and the payment/delivery rule records (oxdelivery, oxdeliveryset, oxpayments, oxobject2payment). Scheduled work is plain PHP scripts invoked by the SYSTEM cron of the hoster - the crontab is outside the repository and must be requested; a script under source/modules/**/cron or bin/ with no caller in the repository is probably cron-driven, not dead. Email-driven business flows sit in oxEmail plus the CMS snippet templates it renders.
snippets.data_script_sources: Doctrine migration up()/down() SQL; metadata.php events onActivate SQL; *.sql files in module setup folders; ERP/PIM import scripts (usually a module command or a cron PHP script writing directly through Doctrine DBAL, bypassing the models - flag those, they skip oxid field validation and cache invalidation); oxid-esales/oxideshop-demodata-* packages for sample data (demo only, never assume it is production data); CSV/XML importers in the admin.
snippets.read_order: root composer.json + composer.lock (compilation, edition, module packages), var/configuration/shops/*.yaml (activation state and effective module settings per shop) and var/configuration/environment/*.yaml, then per module: metadata.php (extend, controllers, templates, blocks, settings, events), services.yaml (DI decoration), migration/, Controller/, Model/, Core/, Service/, then views/ or Application/views (templates and blocks) and translations (*_lang.php / *_options.php), finally vendor/oxid-esales/oxideshop-*/source for the standard class or service actually being extended. Never assert an effective setting from metadata.php alone - the value in var/configuration/shops/<shopId>.yaml wins, and an admin-edited value may exist only there.
snippets.hosting_constraints: self-hosted LAMP or partner-managed hosting - there is no vendor cloud, so every infrastructure fact (PHP version, cron entries, cache backend, file storage, CDN, TLS termination) comes from the hoster and not from the repository; mark those as not verifiable from code. Writable paths are required for source/out (media, generated images), var/ (configuration and cache) and tmp/ - a container or multi-node setup needs shared or object storage for source/out and a cache backend that all nodes share, which many older shops assume is local disk. The file-based template and module-configuration cache must be cleared after any configuration change, so a deployment without a cache-clear step is a real risk to note. Generated database views (oxv_*) must be regenerated after a schema or language change. Enterprise multi-shop requires the EE licence; the licence also gates Visual CMS and the B2B Edition features. A 6.x -> 7.x move is a compilation upgrade: Smarty template overrides, module metadata version and any patched vendor code all need rework.
